items.stem: What does RPO (Recovery Point Objective) specify?

options.text: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
options.rationale: Correct: RPO is how much data, in time, you can afford to lose.

options.text: How long recovery is allowed to take
The number of availability zones in a region
options.rationale: RPO is not about AZ count.

options.text: The cost of the backup vault
options.rationale: RPO is a data-loss target, not a cost.

items.explanation: Correct: RPO is the acceptable data loss in time.

items.stem: Why is a multi-AZ deployment alone insufficient for regional disaster recovery?

options.text: All AZs are within one region, so a regional outage can affect them together
options.rationale: Correct: multi-AZ does not survive a whole-region event.
Multi-AZ improves availability within a region.

items.explanation: Correct: AZs share a region, so cross-region is needed for regional DR.

items.stem: Which TWO strengthen a backup and DR posture on AWS? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Copy backups to a separate region and/or account
options.rationale: Correct: isolation protects against regional or account-level loss.

options.text: Regularly test restores against RTO targets
Keep backups only in the production account and region
options.rationale: Single-location backups are a single point of failure.

options.text: Never test restores to save effort

items.explanation: Correct: isolate backups and test restores.
